title: Circuit breaker benchmarks - scratch
content:
Context:
Quick scratchpad for evening experiments — focusing on the circuit-breaker behavior when upstream model pods slow or OOM and how that affects SLOs and tail latency. Goal: get reproducible microbenchmarks, determine reasonable open/close thresholds for our CB layer, and list follow-ups for a proper playbook entry.

Summary notes (raw):
- Observed: 3 incidents last week where transient GPU OOM + model swap caused p99 spikes to cross 1.2s SLO for 10m windows. Downstream CB didn’t trip fast enough.
- Hypothesis: current CB cooldown and trip counters are tuned for high-throughput stable flakiness, not short sharp capacity drops.
- Experiment plan: synthetic load with controlled per-request latency injection and intermittent 500/502 errors from model-side. Measure CB open rate, fallback engagement, and request loss.

Quick checklist (what I want to run tonight):
- [ ] Reproduce baseline: run bench harness against mainline with no fault injection (rps=400, seq_len=128) — capture p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu util.
- [ ] Inject latency: bench with --inject-latency=200ms on 10% of requests (random) and 50% burst for 10s every 60s.
- [ ] Inject errors: bench with --error-rate=5% returning 502 from model workers.
- [ ] Run same scenarios against branch 'cb/faster-trip' (PR 987) to compare.
- [ ] Record circuit breaker metrics: open_count, open_duration_avg, requests_blocked, fallback_success_rate.
- [ ] Check logs for KV-cache invalidation during model swap (KV cache stamp mismatch).

Commands (local harness):
- bazel run //tools/bench:runner -- --target=http://localhost:8080 --model=redwood-4k --rps=400 --seq=128 --duration=300
- bazel run //tools/bench:runner -- --target=http://localhost:8080 --model=redwood-4k --rps=400 --inject-latency=200 --inject-pct=10 --burst=10s/60s --duration=900
- scripts/compare-cb-logs.sh logs/mainline logs/cb-branch > /tmp/cb-diff.txt

Notes to self on metrics to pull:
- token-per-second breakdown (aggregate + per-route)
- per-pod 95/99 latency and GC pauses
- CB metrics: consecutive_failures, failure_window_size, time_since_open, calls_blocked_by_cb
- fallback model latency (we have a tiny 2B for fast-fallback) and success ratio

Preliminary observations from quick run (today morning):
- Baseline p99 ~ 620ms, with 5-10ms jitter.
- With 200ms injection on 10% random: p99 moved to ~1.05s, tail behavior shows long tails (> 2s) for ~3% of requests when burst coincides with cache miss.
- CB branch PR 987 reduced calls_blocked_by_cb by ~40% but increased open duration slightly — seems threshold logic is more conservative on re-close.

Open questions / decisions:
- What SLO tradeoffs do we accept for short bursts vs sustained degradation? Product prefers fewer dropped requests, infra wants faster fail-open to avoid cascading. Need to align with PM (Zoe) on acceptable fallback rates.
- Should CB track KV-cache state? If cache eviction coincides with slow model load, we get amplified tail — maybe treat cache-miss induced latency as separate signal for CB.
- Should we add a separate fast-path CB for prefix-cache hits? (i.e., if kv-cache=true then CB thresholds are more relaxed)

Action items (owners):
- Sofia: finish reproducible harness scenarios tonight and upload results to Confluence (due 2025-11-04). (blocked by flaky infra on my local cluster; try k8s dev cluster)
- Rajiv: add a small metric export for consecutive_cache_misses per request (JIRA INF-4328).
- Mina: review PR 987 and run perf job on dedicated infra; ping infra for GPU reservations.
- Follow-up: schedule 30m sync with Zoe + Rajiv to pick SLO policy (target next week).

Notes to include in playbook draft later:
- CB policy suggestion: trip when error_rate > 8% OR consecutive_latency_95 > 1.5x SLO for 30s, with exponential backoff to re-close but a forced probe at 10s intervals.
- Fallback policy: prefer fast 2B fallback when CB open; forcibly block heavy requests (>2k tokens).
- Observability: add a dashboard tile for CB state transitions and a synthetic canary that hits CB-protected route every 15s.

Random debug tips / snippets:
- When reproducing, use --seed to make bursts deterministic.
- Use pprof on the handler that proxies to model to see where time is spent during swap (serialize? kqueue?).
- If you see odd 503 spikes, check envoy upstream healthcheck mapping (sometimes envoy marks pod unhealthy early).

Quick log excerpt I pasted earlier (cleaned):
"2025-11-03T09:12:21Z pod-a request-id=... latency=1.27s model=rw-4k cache_hit=false cb_state=CLOSED errors=0"
"2025-11-03T09:12:22Z pod-a request-id=... latency=2.84s model=rw-4k cache_hit=false cb_state=CLOSED errors=1"
"2025-11-03T09:12:23Z pod-a cb_opened reason=consecutive_failures count=5"

Parked ideas (longer term):
- Adaptive CB that uses sequence-length awareness (long sequences are more expensive; treat them differently).
- A tiny admission control token-bucket at the LB that can spill traffic to cheaper region when CB opens.

End-of-scratch notes. Will convert to a short playbook and prod runbook once experiments are reproducible.

-- Sofia
